initial_observation.encounter_context: referred to outpatient clinic from oncology clinic with progressive paraparesis and paresthesia for 1 week (August 2021)
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The patient was diagnosed with Ewing sarcoma approximately 2 years prior, treated surgically and with chemoradiotherapy, considered cured by PET scan 6 months prior; currently presenting with progressive lower limb weakness and sensory deficits with spinal cord lesions on imaging
known_prior_history: Ewing sarcoma diagnosed December 2019 and left clavicular Ewing sarcoma treated surgically with chemotherapy and radiotherapy
Complete metabolic response on PET scan in March 2021

evidence_items.source_text: Emergency whole-spine contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a huge intramedullary thoracic lesion extending from T5 to T8 that was hyperintense in T2-weighted images (Figure 1a), with scattered enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1b). Additionally, there was a round intradural extramedullary mass lesion at the L1 and L2 levels causing a compression effect on the conus medullaris that was isointense in T2-wighted images (Figure 1c), with homogenous enhancement after the injection of contrast (Figure 1d).

On physical examination at the current presentation, the patient’s muscle strength in her lower extremities was as follows: right: 3/5 and left: 1/5 (proximal/distal, respectively). There was a sensory level in the thoracic region (T6), and spastic hyperreflexia was present in the lower extremities (American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) impairment scale C). Urinary sphincter function was intact, but the patient complained of incomplete evacuation of the bladder. A urodynamic study revealed a spastic bladder. Bilateral Babinski reflexes were upward.

Histopathological examination of the thoracic lesion revealed small round cells with moderate pleomorphism, nuclear atypia, and some true rosette formations in a pauci-vascular background (Figure 3a). Immunohistochemical staining of the tumor showed diffuse, strong immunoreactivity for cluster of differentiation (CD)99, and a high proliferative index (Ki-67: 85%–90%), with negative staining for leukocyte common antigen (LCA) (Figure 3b–d). The diagnosis of Ewing sarcoma was confirmed accordingly.
Postoperative imaging of the thoracic spine revealed appropriate decompression (Figure 2a and b) and showed that the lumbosacral lesion had completely resolved (Figure 2c).

At the 10-month follow-up, the patient’s neurological status had worsened, with bilateral lower extremity muscle strength scores of 0/5 (proximal/distal, respectively; ASIA impairment scale B), with spasticity and urofecal retention. She was alive with disease at the time of this report.
